claim: Arc consistency (AC-3) removes values with no support before search; worst-case time is O(e d^2), proven optimal by Zhang and Yap 2001 (older bound O(a^3 e)).
agent_test: Give the agent a constraint list; compare propagate-then-guess against guess-only on grid puzzles at equal tokens.

claim: Strong k-consistency above the constraint-graph width gives backtrack-free search (Freuder); trees need only arc consistency.
agent_test: Order variables by tree-like structure on tree-shaped tasks and count backtracks.

claim: Cost of random CSPs peaks at the soluble/insoluble phase transition (about 50 percent soluble); hard instances sit there.
agent_test: Sample tasks near the transition to test where the scaffold helps; easy tasks hide effects.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: The fail-first heuristic (smallest domain first) is not reliably borne out as predicted; MAC beats forward checking on hard transition problems.
agent_test: Compare smallest-domain-first vs fixed order in the agent's variable choice.

claim: Dynamic backtracking beat backjumping on crossword frames (frame 18: 61 vs 0 of 100; none worse).
agent_test: Allow retracting one assignment without erasing later independent ones; measure solves.

claim: Plain LLMs collapse on CSPs as search space grows: ZebraLogic GPT-4o 31.7 overall, 0.5 X-Large; o1 81.0 overall, 42.5 X-Large; Llama-405B 0.0 X-Large.
agent_test: Run scaffold on ZebraLogic-size bins at equal tokens; report per-bin accuracy.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Sampling and voting give little on large CSPs: GPT-4o majority N=32 38.0 (X-Large 2.5); reward-model best-of-32 34.8; oracle best-of-128 69.1 only with a perfect picker.
agent_test: Equal-token comparison of voting vs propagation-guided search; voting should lose on Large.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Hidden reasoning tokens scale with conflicts (about 5,100-5,350 for o1 vs about 500 for GPT-4o) but plateau above about 30 conflicts.
agent_test: Track tokens per conflict; test whether a systematic loop beats long free reasoning at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Long-chain CSP benchmarks stay hard: LR2Bench best average exact match 23.6 (o1-preview); Sudoku-Bench best single-shot 14.0 (o3-mini-high), 9x9 near 0; SPaRC o4-mini 15.8 vs humans 98.0.
agent_test: Use these as held-out tests of the scaffold.

claim: LLM CSP failures are redundant, unreflective searching and invalid or wrong-constraint states, not only lack of compute (10-gram redundancy negatively correlates with completion).
agent_test: Add a cheap state-validity check each step; count invalid-state outputs.

claim: Self-critique without a sound verifier does not help CSPs: graph colouring 16 percent baseline, 1 of 100 with GPT-4 self-critique, about 40 percent with a sound verifier (same as plain resampling n=15); Game of 24 5 to 3 to 36-38.
agent_test: Replace model self-check with a program that checks constraints; compare at equal tokens.

claim: Offloading CSPs to a solver or code helps a lot: SatLM LSAT 35.0 vs CoT 23.5; ZebraLogic GPT-4o Python 71.7 vs CoT about 30; 3-SAT GPT-4 about 10 to about 100 percent with a solver. Solver-backed small model with exact-cover tool: ZebraLogic 97.9 percent puzzle accuracy vs 91.7 for o3-mini-high plain. Programmatic critics alone (no search solver): TravelPlanner GPT-4-Turbo 4.4 to 20.6 percent.
agent_test: Give the agent a small constraint-check/solver tool; compare to pure text at equal tokens.

claim: Solver gains depend on faithful formalisation: formalizer underperforms the solver in 15 of 24 cases; wrong-constraint errors are 95 percent of Qwen3 semantic errors; accuracy halves on the most constrained problems; declarative prompting without a solver is about standard prompting. The 95 percent comes from an 80-case hand audit (5 per cell). Templated clause translation is far better (SATBench 97 percent faithful); in a solver-tool Zebra pipeline 86 percent of remaining failures are in clue-to-symbol translation.
agent_test: Check translation of each constraint back to words before solving.

claim: Code is not always better: on GSM8K CoT 94.6 beats code 85.8-92.6; retries with Prolog were flat.
agent_test: Gate solver use to constraint-heavy tasks only.

claim: Constraint-programming modelling by LLMs improves with inference-time methods (CPMpy 70.1 to 90.2; MiniZinc 37.8 to 73.2) and agents reach 100 percent on 101 problems; strict multi-instance accuracy is lower (78.3 vs 60.9); retrieved examples sometimes hurt.
agent_test: Model-then-check with multiple instances to avoid overfitting a single example.

claim: More agent overhead is not free: on Haiku 4.5 a todo-list tool raised tokens 191 percent (15K to 44K) and time 111 percent on easy problems, and cut hard-problem success from 52/60 to 45/60 (20 hard problems, 3 runs; it fixed 3 problems and broke 3). Confirmed on re-read.
agent_test: Ablate each scaffold step at equal tokens.

claim: Propagation inside LLM decoding (GenCP) lifts constraint satisfaction: preview depth 2 gave 10 vs 3 solutions on sent-1 and 100 percent satisfaction on reported tasks; beam search was worse.
agent_test: Same-author sources; treat as one team. Replicate with a simple domain-pruning check on output.

claim: Tree of Thoughts with backtracking: crosswords word-level 60 percent vs under 16 for IO/CoT; no-backtrack 20 percent; solved 4 of 20.
agent_test: Ablate backtracking at equal tokens.

claim: LLM-generated streamlining constraints cut search by 98 percent or more on some CSPs in some runs.
agent_test: Ask the agent for extra pruning constraints; verify they keep solutions.

claim: Skills from CSP training transfer: Reasoning Gym games-trained models +21.8 algebra, +13.1 cognition; this attribution is the authors' own.
agent_test: Out of scope for a scaffold, note only.

claim: Explicit algorithm descriptions help little: Sudoku 9x9 8.2 to 12.1; even with code access models reach only 67.2 on Sudoku.
agent_test: Describing the method in prompt is weak; enforce it in the loop.

claim: Dense-constraint tasks collapse early and longer reasoning does not reliably raise correctness (Zebra puzzles: all three reasoning models decline with longer natural reasoning). SATBench hard UNSAT: average model 39.3 percent (below the 50 percent chance), but o4-mini 65.0, DeepSeek-V3 74.3, DeepSeek-R1 83.6. The main error is satisfiability bias.
agent_test: Include UNSAT/impossible items; require the agent to be able to say infeasible.

claim: Gap 2: A programmatic checker with no solver recovers a large relative gain on a non-colouring task: TravelPlanner (180 queries) GPT-4-Turbo 4.4 to 20.6 percent with hand-written critics plus back-prompts (4.6x); GPT-3.5 0 to 5. No matched-token comparison against sampling exists.
agent_test: Build a checker for each constraint class, return the first violated constraint in words, compare to best-of-N at equal tokens.

claim: Gap 3: Wrong-constraint translation is the dominant semantic error in solver pipelines (95 percent of 80 hand-audited Qwen3 errors; 86 percent of 21 solver-tool failures are clue-to-symbol), yet templated clauses translate 97 percent faithfully. Round-trip equivalence checking predicts drift on legal rules (16.2 vs 28.7 percent NLI drift, pooled) but has not been tested on CSP data.
agent_test: Restate each formal constraint in words from the formal form only; mark any mismatch before solving. Measure wrong-constraint rate with and without the step.

claim: Gap 4: Direct reasoning is cheapest on small puzzles and tools pay at large sizes. Qwen3 Plain over 90 percent on small ZebraLogic puzzles, falls sharply on larger; tool pipeline degrades slowly. No study gives a conflict-count threshold. Formalizing itself also halves on the most-constrained 20 percent (10 of 12 pairs).
agent_test: Gate tool or solver use on estimated size (variables times domain). Log where direct reasoning starts failing on our items to set the gate.

claim: Gap 5: Chronological backtracking in a trained model helps on deep-search tasks (Sudoku) and hurts on shallow ones (CountDown). A trained transformer that propagates, makes one guess and backtracks solves 99 percent of random Sudoku, and a single guess suffices for 99.8 percent of boards. Dynamic or selective backtracking in an LLM is untested.
agent_test: Allow retract one assignment and keep independent deductions; cap open guesses at one on propagation-friendly puzzles.

claim: Gap 6: No test of smallest-domain-first as an in-context LLM reasoning rule was found. LLM-written solvers pick first_fail on their own 70.4 percent of the time in MiniZinc and that is largely safe, while other LLM-added search shortcuts cut correctness (median speed-up only 1.03 to 1.12x).
agent_test: Compare fixed order vs smallest-domain-first as a prompt instruction on the same puzzles at equal tokens.

claim: Gap 1 (still open): no measured test of a prompted propagate-then-guess loop at equal tokens. Indirect evidence: long natural reasoning on Zebra puzzles gets worse with length, with short traces showing systematic constraint tracking; ZebraLogic zero-conflict puzzles are solvable by forward chaining alone.
agent_test: Run a three-arm test on ZebraLogic Large and X-Large: plain long reasoning, forced propagation pass then guess, and the same with a checker, all at equal tokens.

claim: Gap 8 (still open): GenCP-style propagation inside decoding has no independent replication found; the IJCAI 2025 paper and its 2024 predecessor come from the same group.
agent_test: Treat as unreplicated; do not build the schema on it.
